newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: BANK AUSTRIA SLOVAK UNIT SAYS TURNS PROFIT IN 1996.
newsitem.headline: BANK AUSTRIA SLOVAK UNIT SAYS TURNS PROFIT IN 1996.

text.p: Bank Austria (SR) a.s., the Slovak unit of Bank Austria, on Wednesday said that according to preliminary figures it posted a 1996 operating profit of 20.14 million crowns, after posting a loss of 6.13 million in 1995.

"Despite the relatively late establishment and relatively small size of the market...we manged to turn around after a mere seven months of operation, breaking even in November," Chairman of the Board Joachim Reitmeier told a news conference.
"We expect similar dynamics of development this year, intending to focus on country's export financing," he added.
The subsidiary's preliminary balance sum totalled 5.38 billion crowns at of the end of 1996, after 1.29 billion crowns in 1995.
The volume of extended loans in 1996, of which three quarters were credits up to one year in maturity, reached 1.9 billion crowns.
Bank Austria (SR), wholly-owned by Bank Austria GmbH, and is registered as a universal bank.
